newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burtundi says Congo to organise Zaire summit.
newsitem.headline: Burtundi says Congo to organise Zaire summit.

text.p: Burundi's military leader Pierre Buyoya said on Saturday Congo was organising a summit on December 2-3 for regional African leaders on the crisis in eastern Zaire.
Buyoya told reporters he would attend the summit after receiving an invitation from Congo's foreign ministry secretary-general Basile Ikouebe in Burundi on Saturday.
Earlier this month Kenya's President Daniel arap Moi organised a summit for East African heads of state to which Burundi was not invited.
Buyoya described as "very, very good" a meeting he held with Uganda's president Yoweri Museveni in Uganda on Friday.
Reuters erroneously reported on Friday that Rwanda's Vice-President and Defence Minister Paul Kagame took part in the talks between Museveni and Buyoya.
The Ugandan presidency confirmed on Saturday that Kagame did not attend the meeting, which was to seek common ground on the crisis in eastern Zaire and sanctions against Burundi.

"I went to Kampala to meet president Museveni to discuss with him the problems of the embargo imposed against Burundi because you know that Uganda was one of the countries to impose sanctions," Buyoya said.
"Relations between Burundi and Tanzania are not good and I asked him to do what he can to normalise these relations."

Diplomats say Burundian Hutu rebels, who fled camps near Uvira in eastern Zaire last month, are fighting their way across Burundi to reestablish bases in western Tanzania, causing a deterioration in relations between the two countries.
Regional states imposed sanctions on Burundi on July 31, six days after Buyoya came to power in a military coup. The presidents of Tanzania and Kenya have refused to see him.
Burundi's leaders, in an effort to gain formal recognition, have conducted a series of meetings with Ugandan and Rwandan leaders and with Tanzanian mediator Julius Nyerere.
